to the latitude of 70°, nor reach the mouth of the riv

bable that this might have been done at another tim.,

rican continents, there is not in any other part.

north-weft
pallage.<x_0.2246><y_0.5398><class_Caption>

<x_0.2354><y_0.4922>With regard to the north-weft pallage, the fame ... ficulties occur as in the other. Captain Cook's voyage
has now affured us, that if there is any fitait which di-
vides the continent of America into two, it muit lie in
a higher latitude than 70°, and consequently be perpe-
tually frozen up. If a north-weft pallage can be found
then, it muit be by failing round the whole American
continent, instead of feeking a pallage through it, which
fome have supposed to exit at the bottom of Baffin's
bay. But the extent of the American continent to the
northward is yet unknown; and there is a profilibility of
its being joined to that part of Afia between the Pialida
and Chatanga, which has never yet been circumnaviga-
ted\*. It remains therefore to confer, whether there
is any polibility of attaining the wilhed-for pallage by
failing directly north, between the eastern and weftern
continents.<x_0.9912><y_0.7148><class_Text>
